body.text:
your-site/
  store/refs/main
  store/log/…
  store/blocks/…
  index.html        loads glass at a pinned version, attaching this store

name: What is named by what it holds
The ref says which commit is current
A commit says how the field came to be this way
A commit across the field's cuts
The table is the whole field at one commit
A version is one holon as it stood
A change adds and never rewrites
Prose held by lone links, until it was holons
The whole keeps them out of sight
A holon is named by itself
A slot and the kind it is
Each value is mounted by what it is
Publishing adds files and moves the ref
A site is a store and a pinned client

body.note: The plan stops at the first mark, so what comes next is not here: the README's Where it stands says it. The first mark's steps and reasons hold as history.
Written before the packs. Has no step for the pack format, the engine on packs or the glass for the human; says none of it is begun, while two of its steps stand under way.
The store is refs/main and packs now: no objects folder, no bundles. True only of the old code in src/store.
No bundle exists; packs read by byte range took its place.
Reversed: objects do not stay loose. The path The store packed, carried by git says what replaced it; packs that never change answer the same worry.
The birth from files ended on 2026-11-06: the holons are the source, and the wiki's files are gone.
Lone links are over: prose is holons, and a reference says it holds, by $holds or by the mould.
Says none of it is built and that a brief is one piece of markdown. In the store prose is native, down to the word. Its reasons hold. The engine does not read it yet.
The vectors pin the loose format, so they no longer say what the store is: the packs answer to none of them, and no test touches packs.ts.
A draft. The store holds paragraph, sentence, word, lexeme, list, item, quote, code, table, closed, link, emphasis, strong and codespan; Term, Image and Ground were not born.
What it says built is the old code, not the store; its markdown prose and a wiki born from files are gone.
Prose made native and the mould are done in the store. What site is built is not unknown: the record and a settled thread say the author's website and CV.
In the packs the tree is keyed by the start of each id, its birth, not the end; the code in src/store still reads from the end.
Name and mould stand in the version in the packs, so not yet built no longer holds for the store; a body with prose as a string is gone. The engine still reads the old shape.
Name and mould are built in the store, not in the engine.
None of this is built no longer holds: the store says holding and the probe follows it. The engine still reads every reference as holding.
Built, and further than it says: holons down to the word. What it costs a client over the network is still unmeasured.
Each object at an address of its own is the loose form; with packs a client reads by range.
Publishing is now a new pack and the ref; no objects uploaded singly, no bundle.
Its layout shows store/objects; a store is packs. The shape of a site holds.
The ref holds a commit and its pack.
A commit in the packs also holds its parent's pack and what it says.
A holon carries its name in its version now; the index still keeps one flat map of names, and routes are not built.
As built, holding not yet said: the store says it by $holds.
The name beside the identity is built in the store, not in the engine.
The mould is built in the store, not in the engine.
Says it is kept in markdown and git: it is in the store, and steps are its data. Its stories hold.
A short lowercase name beside a title is reversed: the title is the name, and no slug stands beside it. Unique within a whole, routes and identity all hold.
Parts are not read from the flow: a brief has a flow of mounts and sections read through after it, and a lone link is no longer how a part is placed.
A brief offering a face to all it holds no longer fits: its sections read through, and what stands in its flow shows its face. The contract of kinds and a slot's own word holds.
